transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-14
Time: 15:00 - 15:52 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Chen (Redwood SE), Lina Ortiz (Redwood CSM), Jordan Lee (NovaHealth Procurement), Priya Kumar (NovaHealth Legal), Dr. Alan Brooks (NovaHealth CTO), Sam Rivera (NovaHealth Security), Marta Gomez (Vendor Ops)

--- Summary (auto-generated) ---
Quick alignment on legal redlines and operational requirements. Action items captured: send MSA/DPA, benchmark spreadsheet, pricing revision, schedule security deep dive.

00:00 Maya Patel: All right, thanks everyone for joining, uh we're, we're on the agenda to walk through the MSA and DPA redlines, SLA expectations for dedicated versus hosted, and pricing approvals. Ethan's going to jump in on the architecture and the benchmark numbers, and then we can go to legal questions.
00:18 Jordan Lee: Great thanks Maya. We only have about an hour so, um, Priya and I are on the line to drive the redlines and then Alan and Sam are here for the infra and security stuff.
00:30 Maya Patel: Perfect. Ethan, do you want to start with a quick overview of the deployment options and where the SLA differences are?
00:38 Ethan Chen: Sure. Uh hi everyone, Ethan here. So at a high level Redwood offers three modes — hosted API, dedicated reserved pool, and private (VPC/on-prem). Hosted is fastest to go live but has shared capacity, so our standard SLA is 99.9 for API availability with best-effort latency targets. Dedicated gives you a dedicated GPU pool with committed throughput and SLA that we can bump to 99.95 or an enterprise SLA depending on contract. Private deployment is the full customer-controlled environment — more integration work, different support terms, and that typically sits under an enterprise license.
01:10 Dr. Alan Brooks: And latency numbers — are those per-model or per-route? We're really sensitive on 99th percentile latency for inference for our triage usecases.
01:20 Ethan Chen: Good question. Our SLA talks to availability; for latency we provide SLOs per-route in the Console — we can set per-model p99 targets and we also have fallback policies to a lower-cost model variant if capacity gets constrained. For dedicated the p99 numbers are typically sub-200ms for our trimmed Llama variants on 80-token requests in our published benchmarks, but we'll attach the full benchmark spreadsheet.
01:45 Sam Rivera: You said KMS/HSM integrations — do you have an HSM option for key material? For private deployments we need HSM-backed keys and customer-managed KMS.
01:56 Ethan Chen: Yes — for Private we support customer-managed KMS; you can plug in your HSM/KMS. For Dedicated we offer integration with major KMS providers and we can support bring-your-own-key in the customer tenancy, plus audit logs. We'll include the KMS doc.
02:12 Priya Kumar: On the DPA — our main concerns are data residency and deletion timelines. We handle PHI in a couple of pilots so we need explicit terms around retention, processing locations and a right-to-delete for training data.
02:28 Maya Patel: Totally understood. Our standard DPA has clauses for processing locations, we can annotate the locations we support and add a retention schedule. For PHI, the Private deployment path is the recommended route but we've seen customers do dedicated pools with contractual assurances.
02:43 Jordan Lee: Procurement question — what is the pricing signoff path? We have to take to finance and then procurement committee. Do you have an approval playbook or typical timelines?
02:53 Maya Patel: Yes, usually we provide a pricing proposal and a commercial term sheet. For Dedicated we often show committed monthly spend tiers; finance usually takes 1-2 weeks, legal another week depending on redlines. We'll provide a pricing ops contact and can expedite if you need a compressed timeline.
03:10 Marta Gomez: For onboarding, what documents do you need from us to start? We need to prep internal intake.
03:15 Lina Ortiz: From Redwood's side we'll need the signed MSA + DPA, a PO or purchase order for Reserved Capacity, and a short onboarding form — we'll supply the checklist in the follow-up.
03:26 Priya Kumar: On MSA redlines — we have a couple of recurring items: indemnity caps, data breach notice timing, and liability carve-outs for third-party models. We also need specific audit rights and SOC 2 Type II evidence.
03:41 Maya Patel: Understood. For indemnity, our standard cap is 1x ARR for most customers but we can discuss based on term and committed spend. For audit evidence we can share SOC2 Type II report and ISO artifacts under NDA — we'll attach the security pack.
03:56 Sam Rivera: Are there any subprocessor lists? We need a full list of subprocessors and the option to review/change them for Private.
04:04 Ethan Chen: We'll include the subprocessors list — for hosted we do have a set of cloud partners; for dedicated and private we can document the stack and provide options for limiting subprocessors in Private.
04:18 Jordan Lee: On SLAs, internal procurement will insist on uptime credits tied to specific metrics. Are credits applied monthly, and how do you calculate them?
04:29 Maya Patel: Credits are typically pro rata against monthly committed fees — we have a service credit table in the MSA. For enterprise agreements we can negotiate custom remedies, but standard language is in the MSA.
04:40 Priya Kumar: We need to check the DPA clause for subprocessors and the right to audit. Also, can you commit to data residency in EU for our EU patient data?
04:51 Ethan Chen: Yes we have region pinning for processing — hosted customers can pick region endpoints; Dedicated can be provisioned in specific cloud regions and Private obviously lives in your VPC/region. We'll note EU-only processing for the EU dataset.
05:05 Dr. Alan Brooks: A technical follow — how do you handle KV cache eviction and warm-start for low latency? If we're using conversational state, we need consistent p95/p99.
05:17 Ethan Chen: We use a KV cache management layer that persists warm cache across requests for session affinity, and we have continuous batching tuned by workload. We'll send a short doc on cache TTLs and warm start heuristics.
05:33 Jordan Lee: Pricing — the quote we received had two lines: hosted per-token plus a reserved capacity chunk. Finance asked about a "dedicated burst" option; is that supported?
05:44 Maya Patel: Yes, we offer burst credits on top of committed capacity for seasonal spikes; we can put that in the SOW as a burst pool or auto-burst policy with defined pricing.
05:52 Priya Kumar: If Redwood's roadmap changes model compatibility, how do you handle compatibility and migration? We need guarantees for API stability.
06:02 Ethan Chen: We version models and provide pinned model versions in the Console; customers can pin a model and we support canary rollouts. For major breaking changes we do a migration window and provide compatibility shims where possible.
06:18 Sam Rivera: Security deep dive scheduling — we need to validate encryption at rest, in transit, and key rotation policies. Also, logging retention and access controls.
06:29 Maya Patel: We'll get our security team on a separate call with Sam — propose next Tuesday and we'll send calendar invite.
06:34 Jordan Lee: On the MSA, Priya's team has a list of 8 high priority redlines — can we get a clean MSA + a diff showing the redlines to make legal review faster?
06:45 Maya Patel: Absolutely — we'll send a clean and a tracked-diff version. We'll also include suggested language for caps and the audit schedule so you can see alternatives.
06:54 Priya Kumar: Two specific asks — 1) a contract clause guaranteeing no model training on NovaHealth data, 2) breach notification within 48 hours. Is that acceptable?
07:06 Maya Patel: No training on customer data is standard; we have contractual language that prohibits training on customer data unless explicitly agreed. For breach notification, standard is 72 hours in our MSA, but we can take 48 hours back to legal — may need to carve depending on breach type. We'll flag as a high-priority redline.
07:22 Dr. Alan Brooks: On compliance evidence — can you provide SOC2 Type II report and pen test summary under NDA?
07:30 Maya Patel: Yes, under NDA we provide SOC2 Type II and an executive pen test summary. We'll include the process to request deeper artifacts.
07:36 Marta Gomez: Operationally — what's the estimated onboarding timeline for a dedicated pool once papers are signed?
07:44 Lina Ortiz: Typically 4-6 weeks for dedicated: 1 week for procurement and contract, 1-2 weeks for infra provisioning and network setup, and 1-2 weeks for integration and validation. Private deployments take longer depending on customer infra.
07:59 Jordan Lee: Is there a pilot option that's timeboxed? We want to run a 6-week pilot with limited capacity to validate latency and quality before committing to a larger pool.
08:10 Maya Patel: Yes, we can structure a timeboxed pilot with a limited reserved pool and a success criteria doc — we can define p99 latency and throughput targets and a go/no-go threshold. That usually helps procurement greenlight.
08:24 Priya Kumar: For the DPA, NovaHealth requires a data processing addendum that explicitly lists subprocessors and subprocessor change notification. We also want indemnity language for regulatory fines stemming from vendor negligence.
08:38 Maya Patel: We'll include subprocessor notifications in the DPA and discuss indemnity carve-outs with legal. For regulatory penalties we're open to negotiating limits and mutual indemnities based on the scope.
08:51 Sam Rivera: One more on network — do you support private link/privatelink equivalents and direct connect for Dedicated?
08:59 Ethan Chen: Yes, we support PrivateLink/direct connect options for Dedicated and Private deployments. We'll include architecture diagrams for both options in the follow-up.
09:12 Jordan Lee: That helps. OK let's talk about timeline — we need internal procurement approval by end of month. That's two weeks. Is that realistic?
09:21 Maya Patel: If you can get back with prioritized redlines in 3 business days, we can try to fast-track — we'll get pricing Ops to produce a revised quote within 3 business days after we get priorities. Legal review may take up to a week after that.
09:33 Priya Kumar: We'll do that. One final question — are there any limitations on model outputs for regulated content? We occasionally need filtering for PHI leaking.
09:45 Ethan Chen: We have content filters and guardrails plus post-processing hooks you can deploy. For PHI-sensitive flows we recommend private or dedicated plus strict filters and monitoring. We'll share the filtering docs.
10:01 Maya Patel: OK, wrapping up. Quick recap and next steps — we'll send clean + diff MSA and DPA, attach SOC2 and subprocessors list under NDA, SE will attach benchmarks and infra diagrams, Pricing Ops will send revised dedicated pricing with burst options, and legal will await NovaHealth's prioritized redlines. We'll also schedule the security deep-dive next week.
10:20 Jordan Lee: Thanks everyone. We'll get the redline list to you by Thursday.
10:25 Priya Kumar: Thanks. Appreciate the SOC2 artifacts and the 48-hour breach flag — we'll call that out.
10:30 Maya Patel: Thanks all, we'll follow up via email with attachments.
10:33 Meeting ends.

--- End of transcript ---
